channel.title: Comments on: Remember the Disease
channel.description: taoism, taoist thought, buddha, yoga, tai chi, shakuhachi

item.title: By: Carl Abbott
item.dc:creator: Carl Abbott
item.description:
Oh no! To the contrary. Your example fits right into this. I was trying to make several points: (too many probably)
(1) Continuous remembering / review favors balance (meta awareness I suppose it's called); (2) In helping others remember, we help ourselves remember; (3) We don't realize we don't know; thus, in youth we need guidance of elders who realize that a little deeper, i.e., who have 'unlearned' enough.

item.title: By: Lynn cornish
item.dc:creator: Lynn cornish
item.description:
People ask us why, when we have twenty plus years sober, we still go to AA meetings. It's because we have good forgetters. We see new people coming in and we are reminded what life used to be like for us. (I notice my husband doesn't remember, but I do!) And we are able to help those newcomers stay sober either by actively working with them, loving them, or just being present as an example.
I hope I haven't obscured your point, that knowing that you don't know is best, in any way.
